h: Purification of the Soul Requires Help From Above

p: הַנּוֹגֵעַ בְּמֵת לְכָל נֶפֶשׁ אָדָם וְגוֹ׳ (בְּמִדְבַּר יט, יא–יב)
"He who touches the dead body of any human being, etc. (Bamidbar 19:11–12),
he shall cleanse himself with it, etc."
the soul of a person who will die"
what is the expression "who will die"?
It should have said "who has died."
מִן כָּל הַנּוֹגֵעַ עַד וְלֹא יִתְחַטָּא
from "Whoever touches" until "and does not cleanse himself"
דְּהָיָה יָכוֹל לְהַתְחִיל אֶת מִשְׁכַּן וְגוֹ׳
for it could have begun with "the Mishkan, etc.,"
to one impure from a dead body
who was not purified with the waters of purification
"He who touches the dead body of any human being,"
refers to the dead person himself,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר אַתֶּם קְרוּיִם אָדָם וְכוּלֵּי
as it says, "You are called adam, etc.";
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בַּנּוֹגֵעַ בְּמֵת נָכְרִי
whereas one who touches a dead gentile
does not become impure according to Rashbi
And this is what it says,
"He shall cleanse himself with it on the third day":
the third day is the third middah,
the aspect of Kudsha Brich Hu;
הַיְינוּ שֶׁיִּתְחַטֵּא עַל יְדֵי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
that is, that he be cleansed through Hashem Yisbarach,
from the side of an awakening from above.
And that is why it says it with the word "Hu,"
because it comes from the side of Hashem Yisbarach.
And this is the preparation for the seventh day,
which indicates the middah of Malchus;
that is, the effort from the person
and through this he will become pure.
And "if he does not cleanse himself on the third day"
from the side of Hashem Yisbarach,
from the side of the person,
the soul of a person who will die"
זֶה בְּנֶפֶשׁ הָאָדָם קָאֵי עַל הַנּוֹגֵעַ
this "soul of a person" refers to the one who touches,
who is a soul of a person of Yisrael,
"and does not cleanse himself" in this world,
דְּאִם הָיָה מְקַבֵּל עוֹנְשׁוֹ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
for had he received his punishment in this world,
all those liable to kares who received lashes
and does not cleanse himself" through others,
that is, from the side of Hashem Yisbarach,
not having received his punishment in this world
"he has defiled the Mishkan of Hashem,
and that soul shall be cut off, etc."
וּלְהַלָּן כְּתִיב עוֹד הַפַּעַם (שָׁם יט, כ)
And further on it is written once again (Bamidbar 19:20),
"And a man who becomes impure and does not cleanse himself,
that soul shall be cut off, etc."
there it is written "from among the congregation,"
and here it is written "shall be cut off, etc., from Yisrael";
and there it is written "he is impure,"
and here it is written "he shall be impure;
his impurity is still upon him"
and these words are entirely superfluous.
But it is as we said,
"the soul of a person who will die,"
refers to the one who touches.
And it is written "the soul of the person,"
and that is the great person;
for there are several levels among the names:
"adam," the greatest of them all is "adam,"
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג מח, א)
And this is that even with the soul of the great person
that is, that the yetzer hara entered him
which is what the root of death indicates,
And if he will die afterward
and not be cleansed in this world
"he has defiled the Mishkan of Hashem":
that is, the heart, which is called the Mishkan of Hashem,
Who dwells in the heart of Yisrael;
and he did not let the holiness
dwell in the heart of Yisrael.
the upper hei and the lower hei,
which shines from the root, the alef,
that is, he will not be able to merit
and with men, and have prevailed."
And this is what it says, "he shall be impure":
מוֹרֶה עַל יוֹד שֶׁל שֵׁם שַׁדַּי
indicates the yud of the Name Shakai,
which shines to the last hei.
from the side of Hashem Yisbarach,
and then he will return to the level of Yisrael.
which speaks of a lower level of Yisrael;
and this is why it says "and a man,"
which is a lower level than "adam":
that soul shall be cut off"
the word "hahi" is explained as above;
And it is written "from the midst of the congregation,"
which indicates the inner aspect of Knesses Yisrael:
in the midst of Bnei Yisrael,
and even when they are impure
כִּי אֶת מִקְדַּשׁ ה׳ טִמֵּא וְגוֹ׳
"For he has defiled the Sanctuary of Hashem, etc.;
and he will need other refinements,
so that he not be cast out from the congregation of Yisrael,
who have a share in the World to Come.
